: Jim Evans took up athletics only at the beginning of this season and was introduced to Belgrave by John Bicourt. Expecting to gradually get fit and have a real go next year, he was immediately thrown in at the deep end with a 100m run in our first league match in May and has regularly been a membe…

Newcomer Jim Evans showed a flash of great things to come in the 'B' 100 metres. Last away, he rocketed through the field and then just faded a little in the final 10 metres - a good performance, particularly as he has only just taken up the sport with a mere three weeks training behind him.

With Steve White and John Bicourt selected to compete at the British International Games on the same day our hopes took a tumble, and when sprinter Jim Evans became ill the day before the meeting all thoughts of winning had gone - it was to be a fight to avoid a real hammering.

Steve White again picked up maximum score in each of his events and he was backed up by Jim Evans, equalling his 11.3 best again, and Martin Scott who does us great service by regularly turning out and cruising below his best with that nagging leg injury.

Only fifteen minutes after strolling into the arena Jim Evans was on the blocks for the 100m. With virtually no warm-up he did all that was asked of him and more, finishing 2nd behind the 10.7 of the Hillingdon runner and surely much closer to him than his 11.3 suggested.

Highlights included 22.9 for Charlie Gillett and 23.1 for Jim Evans over 200m, 49.8/400 Steve White, sub-50 from Steve and Charlie in the 4x400, 14:35.0/5000 from John Stow, 13.21/TJ from Steve Crosbie, 3.35/PV from Reg Hopkins ................................

This left a gap in the shorter sprints but Jim Evans was encouraged to run his first ever 200m by the persuasive Snowy Brooks and a 23.1 debut ensured that the 'B' 200 was his for the rest of the season.
Now used to the idea of 200m, Jim Evans was given something else to think about - the long jump. Sheer speed and little technique got him to 6.59 for a good 'B' win.
Jim Evans won his 'B' 100m taking advantage of that same wind, clocking a personal best of 11.1, the same time as Steve White in the 'A' race.
Looking sharper every time he runs, Jim Evans was obvious favourite for the 100m and he duly broke the tape in 11.3, equalling his own and championship bests.
We look forward to Jim Evans' 1976 season with great interest. Last year, his first in athletics, he gave us some exciting runs improving as the summer wore on.

With injury still hampering him Jim Evans was unable to give Ernest Obeng a real fight in the men's 100m. but even without pressure Ernest sped to a time of 10.9, four tenths inside the previous championship best.

Last year Jim Evans turned up, filling a vacant place and now developing into a really good sprinter. This year, no sooner than Steve White had transferred to Oxford, Ernest Obeng from Ghana began to clock remarkable times in Belgrave colours.

This was the day of Jim Evans' first real test after a winter of hard determined training, and after a long afternoon of competition in gusty conditions the grin on his face betrayed that he had succeeded beyond even his own wildest dreams.
(For record purposes a following wind should not exceed 2.0 metres per second). Jim Evans in heat three did not look comfortable under the severe pressure of a A.A.A. heat and clocked 11.13 for 5th.
Having recovered from his knee injury Jim Evans took both 'B' sprints again and he also is unbeaten in the league although missing out on a couple of 200s.

Congratulations to James Evans who was voted the most outstanding athlete at the 1976 Surrey County Championships. The Officers and Committee of Belgrave Harriers wish all members and their families a very Happy Christmas and a successful New Year.
Stretching their unbeaten series of league sprints from one year to the next, Ernest Obeng and Jim Evans looked superb, with Ernie drawing gasps from the spectators each time he went into action.

Our double champion from last year's meeting, Jim Evans, has been finding things tough recently with injuries, moving home, etc. but Belgrave's colours were kept to the fore in the sprints thanks to Ernest Obeng, competing in his first "Surrey".

Jim Evans backed up as reliably as ever in the 'B' sprints. John Bicourt turned out to give us a 5000m/1500m double and Ian Duncan, fitting into our team very nicely, scored well in the 'B' 1500, but again the most exciting race was the 4 x 400 metres relay.
International Les Hoyte (Thames Valley) was awarded the silver medal with our Jim Evans in 5th place but sharing the same time, 10.8, as Hoyte.
Jim Evans was also in good form with 10.9 and 22 second sprints, and Martin Scott celebrated his return to our league team by winning the long jump.

Once again our sprinters scored heavily with Jim Evans, Kunle Ashaye and Derrick Williams looking really good, when it came to the relay they scorched to a magnificent 42.6 for second fastest time ever in Belgrave history - and that without Ernest Obeng.

Ernest Obeng put us into the lead from the start, Derrick Williams carried the clubs colours down the back straight, but as Charlie Gillett came off the final bend he had a sudden attack of cramp and Jim Evans had to slow down to get the baton.
Jim Evans broke 11 seconds in coming second in the A 100 and Steve Crosbie broke 13m on the triple jump for the first time in three years. Overall yet another fourth place for the team.
Two of our members - sprinter Jim Evans and javelin thrower Peter Crosbie - have quit our side for that of Epsom & Ewell H. and National League Competition.
